subject: common-workplace-fundamentals
summary: Explains Git basic commands, commit message reading, and fundamental branch strategy for workplace collaboration.
key_points: Understand the role of add, commit, push, pull in the Git workflow.
Read commit messages to identify change intent and scope.
Use feature branches to keep the main branch stable.
misconceptions: A one-word commit message like 'fix' is sufficient.
Working directly on main branch is acceptable for small changes.
Conflicts can be resolved by always accepting your own changes.
check_questions: What is the difference between git add and git commit?
Why is a feature branch strategy important?
What makes a commit message useful for future investigation?

fact_candidates: Role of each Git basic command in the workflow
practical_judgment_candidates: Deciding when to create a separate branch
error_interpretation_candidates: Understanding merge conflict markers and resolution
scenario_candidates: Vague commit message with no context
Conflict after pushing without pulling first
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Assuming direct main branch work is safe
